modules.module: M1: Where AI Actually Enters the Design Process

Claude.notes: The BIG Shenzhen opener creates the exact problem the lesson resolves — expand the search space vs. make the design decision — and that through-line carries through every subsequent stage. Vocabulary and cognitive framing are properly pitched for licensed architects.
Claude.topIssue: Lab is chat-based rather than a hands-on run of Forma or Insight, so the applied capability delta rides on the tutor's responsiveness rather than observable tool use.

Gemini.notes: Definitions of generative design, LLM-assisted specification, and computer vision in CA are technically sound. Named firms, tools, and launch dates (Forma 2022, UpCodes AI 2022) check out. Specific quantitative claims are harder to verify.
Gemini.topIssue: The NBBJ '34 percent more errors caught / 11 percent false positives' figure anchors the quiz but is not independently traceable to a published NBBJ case study.

Perplexity.notes: Tools cited (Forma, Insight, OpenSpace, UpCodes AI) remain active and current. The 'AIA 2023 Firm Survey — 42 percent AI adoption' anchors most of the macro framing and will need refresh when the next AIA Firm Survey lands.
Perplexity.topIssue: The lesson's reference window is 2022–2023; 2024–2025 shifts (Autodesk Forma pricing/feature changes, Spacemaker rebrand into Forma, EU AI Act commencement) are deferred to Module 8 and absent here.

Claude.notes: Rotterdam 2014 opener earns the 'designer defines the problem, algorithm proposes' pivot cleanly. The parametric-vs-generative distinction and the Stiny → Frazer → Dreamcatcher → Spacemaker lineage give learners a durable mental model rather than a tool catalogue.
Claude.topIssue: The problem-formulation lab stays abstract; a hands-on Grasshopper/Galapagos or Testfit mini-exercise would make the 'authoring the rules that govern geometry' claim provable.

Gemini.notes: Technical scaffolding is sound: Stiny and Gips (1972), SIMP via Bendsøe and Kikuchi (1988), Spacemaker's 2020 Autodesk acquisition at ~$240M, and the Pareto/EA/gradient taxonomy are correct. Bloomberg bracket topology optimisation attribution to Arup is accurate.
Gemini.topIssue: The Skanska Oslo '18% higher average daylight / 4% construction-cost reduction' figures are specific enough to invite verification but no citation to a Skanska or Spacemaker whitepaper is given.

Perplexity.notes: The tool landscape (Galapagos, Octopus, Autodesk Generative Design, Hypar.io, Testfit.io) remains broadly accurate as of 2025–2026. The 2025 maturation of ML-accelerated solvers (nTopology, Rhino WIP ML tools) is not referenced.
Perplexity.topIssue: Treats Spacemaker as a standalone product; since 2023 Autodesk has largely folded Spacemaker's capabilities into Forma, which is how practitioners encounter it today.

modules.module: M3: How Machines Learned to Draw Rooms

Claude.notes: The Dreamcatcher opener and 'did it know the sun moves?' anecdote create a crisp framing of what 'generate' actually means. The three-generation-methods taxonomy (parametric / GAN / diffusion) with distinct failure modes gives learners the diagnostic vocabulary they need to interrogate any floor-plan tool.
Claude.topIssue: The ETH Zürich / Liane Müller 'hard adjacency constraint graph' scene is unattributed to a published source and reads as composite — fine as pedagogy but should be flagged as illustrative.

Gemini.notes: The parametric / stochastic / diffusion taxonomy is correct and the Chaillou ArchiGAN (Harvard GSD) attribution is accurate. However, HouseGAN is attributed to Tsinghua University in 2019; the HouseGAN paper (Nauata et al., ECCV 2020) was principally authored at Simon Fraser University with Yasutaka Furukawa, not Tsinghua in 2019. The '145,000 floor plans' corpus description is also not consistent with the HouseGAN RPLAN dataset of record.
Gemini.topIssue: HouseGAN's attribution and publication year are factually off, which matters because the quiz tests the specific claim.

Perplexity.notes: The diffusion-floor-plan ecosystem has moved rapidly: Maket.ai, Architect AI, Rayon.design, and finetuned Stable Diffusion / SDXL pipelines are the current frontier, and the lesson captures that well. The specific Maket.ai beta figures (40% constraint-time overhead, 3× initial-layout output) read as plausible but are not externally sourced.
Perplexity.topIssue: Does not discuss the newer wave of LLM+constraint pipelines (ChatGPT/Claude as the constraint-authoring interface over a geometric backend) that dominated 2024–2025 architectural press.

modules.module: M4: Topology Optimization and Generative Form

Claude.notes: Frei Otto's 1972 soap-film opener earns the 'form-finding ↔ topology optimization' bridge beautifully; the Airbus A320 bracket and MX3D bridge land the aerospace-to-architecture transfer. The 'algorithm finds the physics; the architect finds the architecture' line is the module's keeper.
Claude.topIssue: The sports-hall lab is well-scoped but still conversational; a referenced Grasshopper/Karamba3D or Fusion 360 Generative Design file would turn the stated capability delta into something auditable.

Gemini.notes: SIMP, volume fraction, and the design-space / load-case vocabulary are all correctly specified. However, this module says the MX3D Bridge was 'completed 2021', while Module 1 describes it as 'the 2019 pedestrian bridge in Amsterdam' — the bridge was fabricated 2015–2018 and publicly installed in July 2021, and the course should pick one framing.
Gemini.topIssue: Internal inconsistency on the MX3D Bridge date between M1 and M4; a quiz learner moving across modules will see conflicting dates.

Perplexity.notes: Autodesk Generative Design in Fusion 360 and the Karamba3D / Grasshopper workflow remain current. Embodied carbon tooling (One Click LCA, Tally, EC3, Beacon) has moved fast since 2024 and is only lightly referenced in L3.
Perplexity.topIssue: Embodied-carbon databases cited (EC3, ICE) continue to update their underlying EPDs, and the specific 22% embodied-carbon reduction figure from the Arup atrium study needs refresh to reflect post-2024 EPD methodology.

modules.module: M5: Sunlight, Shadow, and the Algorithm

Claude.notes: The Shard shadow controversy opening is the strongest cold-open in the course — it reframes 'compliance' as a lived urban failure, and the shift to CBDM / UDI / ASE answers it on the correct register. The surrogate-model concept lands with the right level of mathematical honesty for the audience.
Claude.topIssue: Four large physical domains (solar, wind, thermal, acoustics + flood) are packed into one module; L4 in particular feels compressed and the module would read better split or trimmed.

Gemini.notes: Radiance (LBNL, from 1985), EnergyPlus, LEED v4 ASE threshold (10% of occupied hours above 1,000 lux), Lawson wind-comfort categories, and the Navier-Stokes / RANS / LES / PINN framing are all technically correct. The Edge Amsterdam BREEAM 98.36% figure is accurate.
Gemini.topIssue: The specific 'ETH Zurich 2020 CNN trained on 20,000 urban CFD simulations, MAE 6.3%' claim is specific enough that it should name the paper (likely the Patro / Giustozzi / Masoero-adjacent surrogate work, or similar), and does not.

Perplexity.notes: Ladybug Tools, Radiance, EnergyPlus and the Grasshopper surrogate workflow remain the live stack through 2025–2026. PINN research has continued (NVIDIA Modulus, DeepXDE), so framing PINNs as 'frontier' is still accurate.
Perplexity.topIssue: The LEED v4 reference will go stale when LEED v5 is finalized; the lesson does not flag the imminent transition that practitioners are already preparing for.

modules.module: M6: Smart Cities and Urban Data Infrastructure

Claude.notes: Sidewalk Toronto, Songdo, and Barcelona CityOS form a three-case triad that lets the learner derive the governance taxonomy themselves rather than being handed it. The 'who decides what gets optimized' through-line is one of the sharpest in the course, and the architect-as-data-governance-actor framing in the gold callout is exactly the move an Advanced course should make.
Claude.topIssue: The lab asks the learner to counsel a mid-size city on data strategy, but offers no concrete deliverable (a one-page governance brief, a sensor-type matrix) to show for the exchange.

Gemini.notes: The verifiable spine is strong: Sidewalk Labs withdrawal (May 2020), Cavoukian resignation (October 2018), Barcelona DECODE / Decidim under Colau and Bria, Surtrac from CMU (Smith & Barlow), SCOOT / SCATS deployments, Cruise's October 2023 permit suspension by the California DMV, and Helsinki's Whim all check out.
Gemini.topIssue: The FIWARE 'federated-commons model' framing is more aspirational than operational; FIWARE is largely a middleware specification rather than a governance regime, and the lesson slightly overstates its scope.

Perplexity.notes: Cruise's post-October-2023 trajectory — GM pulling the robotaxi business and discontinuing Cruise driverless operations in late 2024 — is not reflected; the lesson still treats the Waymo/Cruise comparison as live. Barcelona's post-Colau administration has partially rolled back the data-sovereignty posture, which also goes unmentioned.
Perplexity.topIssue: The AV section reads as of mid-2023 and misses the Cruise shutdown and Waymo's 2024–2025 expansion to Austin, Atlanta, Miami — all directly relevant to the 'adaptive zoning' argument.

modules.module: M7: 3D Scanning and Photogrammetry at Scale

Claude.notes: The Mosul/Nimrud opener and the Palmyra Arch replica debate are the course's strongest moral framing, and the London Charter / Seville Principles / Bamiyan Buddhas sequence lets the learner build an ethical position rather than inherit one. The 'point clouds are not models' distinction is the kind of operator-grade knowledge that justifies the Advanced level.
Claude.topIssue: Lab 1 (72-hour bridge documentation) is scenario-rich but still conversational; a sketched scan-station plan on a plan of the bridge would make the capability delta concrete.

Gemini.notes: Andrew Tallon's Notre-Dame scan (c. 2010–2017, approx. 1 billion points), PointNet (Qi et al., Stanford, 2017), CyArk's Skara Brae resurvey, the London Charter (2009) and Seville Principles (2012) all check out. ICAHM / ICOMOS attribution for the Seville Principles is correct.
Gemini.topIssue: The specific KPConv Zurich Old Town figure ('1.4 billion points into 23 semantic classes') and the Nathalie Sibieude 2022 INP fresco-completion study are specific-sounding but not externally linked; both would need citation to survive technical audit.

Perplexity.notes: The tool stack (Agisoft Metashape, RealityCapture, CloudCompare, point-cloud ML frameworks) remains current. NeRF framing is correct but 3D Gaussian Splatting — which has become the dominant 2024–2025 approach for photorealistic scene reconstruction in heritage work — is not mentioned.
Perplexity.topIssue: Omits Gaussian Splatting, which has largely eclipsed NeRF for heritage photogrammetry since late 2023 and is the technique a 2026 practitioner would reach for first.

modules.module: M8: Authorship, Liability, and the New Legal Terrain

Claude.notes: The AL_A Riyadh story and the fractured-authorship framing earn their rhetorical weight — the module takes a genuinely hard question and gives the learner a working legal vocabulary (duty of care, instrument of service, high-risk AI). The pivot to curatorial skill and task compression closes the course well.
Claude.topIssue: The 'strategic positioning' section (L4) reads a touch like management consulting pitching to architects; a shorter, sharper version with one case rather than a positioning matrix would land harder.

Gemini.notes: AIA Document B101, NCARB practice advisories, the Spanish City of Culture of Galicia parametric litigation reference, EU AI Act high-risk classification, California SB 1047 veto, and NAAB 2020 Conditions are all broadly accurate.
Gemini.topIssue: The claim that Victor Insurance and 'Berkley One's architecture division' have specifically added AI-use disclosure fields to renewal applications since 2022 is stated with the precision of a market report but no insurer document or carrier letter is cited.

Perplexity.notes: The EU AI Act timeline (entered force August 2024, high-risk obligations phased through 2026–2027) and the Newsom SB 1047 veto (September 2024) are current. RIBA's 2024 AI working group is a real body; its draft principles continue to evolve into 2026.
Perplexity.topIssue: The AIA, NAAB, and NCARB positions are moving targets; the lesson should flag that any specific document reference may be superseded by a newer edition (NAAB 2026 Conditions, ARE restructuring work still in progress).
